</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Soy, as sold from all 25 cultivars, field soil 1.22 mg Cd/kg (experiment) had cadmium higher at 470 µg/kg, against 180 µg/kg for soybean cultivar Hefeng 40, control soil in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/zhi2020-soybean-cadmium-safe-cultivars|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Zhi Y, Sun T, Zhou Q, Leng X · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/zhi2020-soybean-cadmium-safe-cultivars">Screening of safe soybean cultivars for cadmium contaminated fields</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports 10:12965</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/zhi2020-soybean-cadmium-safe-cultivars">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot results with a quantification limit well below the limit that applies in the destination market.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/andrade2023-cow-milk-soy-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Vanda Lopes Andrade, Iolanda Ribeiro, A. P. Marreilha dos Santos, Michael Aschner, Maria Luisa Mateus · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/andrade2023-cow-milk-soy-metals">Metals in Cow Milk and Soy Beverages: Is There a Concern?</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/andrade2023-cow-milk-soy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fsa2014-infant-foods-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Food Standards Agency, Hallmark Meat Hygiene · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fsa2014-infant-foods-metals">Survey of metals and other elements in commercial infant foods, infant formula and non-infant specific foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Standards Agency report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fsa2014-infant-foods-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Marín S, Pardo O, Sánchez A, Sanchis Y, Vélez D, Devesa V, Font G, Yusà V · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals">Assessment of metal levels in foodstuffs from the Region of Valencia (Spain)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 5 (2018) 654-670</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/marin2018-valencia-foodstuffs-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the soy came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-soy" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-soy-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of soy, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach soy

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach soy comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Soy, as sold from soybean cultivar Hefeng 40, pot soil spiked to 2.5 mg Cd/kg (T2) (experiment) had cadmium higher at 2,060 µg/kg, against 180 µg/kg for soybean cultivar Hefeng 40, control soil in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/zhi2020-soybean-cadmium-safe-cultivars|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Zhi Y, Sun T, Zhou Q, Leng X · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/zhi2020-soybean-cadmium-safe-cultivars">Screening of safe soybean cultivars for cadmium contaminated fields</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports 10:12965</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/zhi2020-soybean-cadmium-safe-cultivars">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, soy, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in WPRO (4 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (50 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (1.17 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (130 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Targeted soy, as sold samples in WPRO had cadmium lower at 2.05 µg/kg, against 20 µg/kg for WPRO in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, targeted soy, as sold samples in WPRO had cadmium higher at 50 µg/kg, against 20 µg/kg for WPRO in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>
## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="hmi-ing-022"></a>
<a id="can-an-intervention-increase-another-contaminant-or-redistribute-contamination-to-a-by-product"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-023"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-024"></a>
<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/zhi2020-soybean-cadmium-safe-cultivars|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Zhi Y, Sun T, Zhou Q, Leng X · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/zhi2020-soybean-cadmium-safe-cultivars">Screening of safe soybean cultivars for cadmium contaminated fields</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports 10:12965</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/zhi2020-soybean-cadmium-safe-cultivars">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.



<a id="sampling-and-testing"></a>
## Testing soy for metals

<a id="hmi-ing-025"></a>
<a id="what-sampling-design-is-appropriate-for-the-ingredient-heterogeneity-lot-and-decision"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-026"></a>
<a id="which-methods-species-measurements-validation-evidence-and-reporting-limits-are-needed"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-027"></a>
<a id="what-can-a-certificate-of-analysis-or-non-detect-establish-and-what-remains-untested"></a>

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead ranged from 0.04 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food) to 25,000 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Reporting limits for cadmium ranged from 0.4 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food) to 100 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Reporting limits for total arsenic ranged from 2.5 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food) to 997 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

A useful lot result names the form, the basis and a quantification limit well below the limit that applies.

## Soy FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-soy" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-soy" data-question="What heavy metals are found in soy?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in soy?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, As, Hg, I, Li, Mo and Sr in soy, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/andrade2023-cow-milk-soy-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Vanda Lopes Andrade, Iolanda Ribeiro, A. <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-soy" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-soy" data-question="How do heavy metals get into soy?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into soy?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, soy from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than soy from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/zhi2020-soybean-cadmium-safe-cultivars|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Zhi Y, Sun T, Zhou Q, Leng X · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/zhi2020-soybean-cadmium-safe-cultivars">Screening of safe soybean cultivars for cadmium contaminated fields</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports 10:12965</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/zhi2020-soybean-cadmium-safe-cultivars">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Soy, as sold from all 25 cultivars, field soil 1.22 mg Cd/kg (experiment) had cadmium higher at 470 µg/kg, against 180 µg/kg for soybean cultivar Hefeng 40, control soil in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/zhi2020-soybean-cadmium-safe-cultivars|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Zhi Y, Sun T, Zhou Q, Leng X · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/zhi2020-soybean-cadmium-safe-cultivars">Screening of safe soybean cultivars for cadmium contaminated fields</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports 10:12965</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/zhi2020-soybean-cadmium-safe-cultivars">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-soy" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-soy" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in soy?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in soy?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, soy, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in WPRO (4 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (50 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (1.17 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (130 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
